questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **an outcome of endogenic forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sea waves**__.

__
 
• **Sea waves are not an outcome of endogenic forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Endogenic forces**:

 
 
• These forces are also called **Internal Forces**.
 
• The forces originating in the interior of the earth are called the internal or the endogenic forces.
 
• Volcanic eruptions, Earthquakes, and Landslides are examples of internal forces.
 
 
 
• **Exogenic Forces:**
 
 
• These forces are also called **External Forces.**
 
• The **forces affecting the surface of the earth from outside** are called the external or exogenic forces.
 
• Weathering and Erosion are examples of external forces.
 
 
 
• **Sea waves are the outcomes of wind and gravitational energy.**

questions.question: How many arteries are there in an umbilical cord?

• The cord **transports nutrients** to the baby and also** carries away the waste products** of the baby.
 
• The cord is made up of **two arteries and one vein.**
 
 
 
• **Arteries **carry **pure blood from the heart** to other parts of the body.
 
• **Veins **carry** impure blood to the heart.**

• It is slightly **alkaline in nature**.

• Its **volume **in an **adult human is 5.8 L**.
 
• **Plasma**:
 
 
• This is the **liquid part of blood.**
 
• **60% of the blood is plasma.**
 
• **90% part of the blood plasma is water, 7% protein, 0.9% salt, and 0.1% is glucose.**
 
 
 
• **Blood corpuscles:**
 
 
 
• The remaining **40% part of the blood** is made of corpuscles

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides power to the President for promulgating ordinances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 123**__.

__
 
• **Article 123 of the Constitution of India provides power to the President for promulgating ordinances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President**:

 
 
• President is the** head of the Union Executive.**
 
• He is indirectly elected by an electoral college, in accordance with the system of **proportional representation **by means of the **single transferable vote.**
 
• **Qualifications:**
 
 
• **​**He should be a **citizen of India.**
 
• He should have **completed 35 years of age.**
 
• He should be **qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha**.
 
• He should not hold any office of profit under the Union Government or any State Government or any local authority or any other public authority.
 
• Article 60 deals with the Oath and Affirmation of the President.
 
 
 
• The oath of the President is administered by the **Chief Justice of India** and in his absence, **the seniormost Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• According to **Article 56**, the President shall hold office for a** term of five years** from the date on which he enters his office.
 
• **Article 123** of the Constitution of India **provides power to the President for promulgating ordinances.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 143 **empowers the **President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court**.

 
 
• The SC is bound to give its **opinion **which is **not binding on President**.
 
 
 
• **Article 77 **states that all the **executive action** of the **Government of India shall be done in the name of the President**.
 
• **Article 111** states that the President shall declare his assent to a bill passed by both the Houses of Parliament or withhold his assent, provided he returns the bill to Parliament for reconsideration.

questions.question: Carbon and energy requirements of an autotrophic organism are fulfilled by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**photosynthesis**__.

__
 
• **The carbon and energy requirements of an autotrophic organism are fulfilled by photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**:

 
 
• In the presence of water, light, chlorophyll, and carbon dioxide, the **formation of carbohydrates **in the plant is called **photosynthesis**.
 
• The carbon and energy requirements of an autotrophic organism are fulfilled by this process.
 
• Terrestrial plants take CO₂ from the atmosphere whereas aquatic plants use carbon dioxide mixed in water.
 
• Water enters into cells of the leaves through **osmosis **and **CO****₂**** through diffusion** from the atmosphere or released during respiration.
 
• The **green colour of the plants** is due to the presence of **chlorophyll**. 
 
• There is an **atom of magnesium** in the center of **chlorophyll**.
 
• Chlorophyll absorbs the **violet, blue, and red colour of light**.
 
• The** rate of photosynthesis is maximum in red light **and is **minimum in violet light.**
 
• The process of photosynthesis is a **reaction of oxidation and reduction**.

• **Hindu Rate of Growth:**

 
 
• The term was coined by** Professor Rajkrishna **in the year **1978**.
 
• The average growth of GDP during the period was around 3.5% while per capita income grew by an **insignificant 1.3%**.
 
• The country's annual population growth rate was over 2% in the 1980s.

• The term “***Hindu***” was used by some early economists to indicate that the Hindu outlook of **acceptance and contentedness** was responsible for the slow growth.

questions.question: Lymph is a light clear fluid made up of white blood cells that attack harmful _______ in the blood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteria**__.

__
 
• **Lymph is a light clear fluid made up of white blood cells that attack harmful bacteria in the blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lymph Circulatory System**

 
 
• The** light yellow fluid **found in the intercellular spaces between different tissues and cells is called lymph.
 
• The corpuscles found in the lymph are called **lymphocytes**.
 
• Lymph flows only in one direction from the **tissue towards the heart**.
 
• **Functions of Lymph**
 
 
• Lymph forms the lymphocytes.
 
• The lymphocytes present in lymph help prevent the body from disease by killing the **harmful bacteria.**

• **Diseases caused by bacteria:**

 
 
• Diphtheria, pneumonia, cholera, tetanus, tuberculosis, plague, and gonorrhea.
 
 
 
• **Diseases caused by fungi:**
 
 
• Ringworm and athlete's foot.
 
 
 
• **Diseases caused by protozoa:**
 
 
• Malaria, Dysentery, Diarrhea, Kala Azari.
